content.text: {"concept_key":"c5-maths-addition","title":"Addition","quick":"Addition means putting two groups together to find the total. Count both groups together, starting from the bigger number.","full":"Imagine Ishika buys 9 toffees from the kirana shop, then her friend gives her 3 more toffees. To find the total, she does not need to count all from 1. She starts at 9 and counts forward 3 more: 10, 11, 12. So 9 + 3 = 12. Addition always means combining two amounts into one bigger amount.","tip":"Start counting from the bigger number and add on the smaller one: 9...10,11,12.","answer":"12","traps":["Counting both numbers from 1 instead of starting from the bigger one","Miscounting on fingers and landing one number short or extra","Confusing addition with subtraction and taking away instead of combining"],"misconception":"Child thinks every sum must be counted from 1, 2, 3... instead of starting from the bigger number and counting on.","parent_questions":[{"q":"If you have 9 pencils and I give you 3 more, how do you find the total without counting from 1?","expected_answer_hint":"Start at 9 and count 10, 11, 12 to get 12."},{"q":"What does the + sign tell us to do with two numbers?","expected_answer_hint":"It tells us to combine or put the two groups together to find the total."}],"check_question":{"q":"7 + 4 = ____","options":["11","10","12"],"correct_index":0,"right_feedback":"Correct! 7 and 4 combined make 11.","wrong_feedback":"Not quite. Start at 7 and count on 4 more: 8, 9, 10, 11."},"illustration":{"scene_prompt":"A girl at a small kirana shop counting toffees in her hand while the shopkeeper hands her a few more.","labels":[]}}
